description: Physical symptoms experienced during perimenopause and menopause

entries.title: Hot Flashes
entries.description: Sudden waves of heat, redness, and sweating, often felt in the face, neck, and chest
entries.content: Hot flashes are one of the most common symptoms of menopause, affecting up to 75% of women. They are sudden feelings of intense warmth that spread over the body, particularly the face, neck, and chest. Episodes can last from 30 seconds to several minutes and may be accompanied by flushing, sweating, and rapid heartbeat. Hot flashes are caused by changes in the hypothalamus (the body's thermostat) due to declining estrogen levels.
entries.duration: Can last for several years, often intensifying during late perimenopause
management: Dress in layers and wear breathable fabrics like cotton
Avoid triggers like caffeine, alcohol, spicy foods
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If hot flashes are severe, disruptive to daily life, or accompanied by unexplained weight loss

entries.title: Night Sweats
entries.description: Episodes of excessive sweating during sleep that can soak bedding
entries.content: Night sweats are hot flashes that occur during sleep, causing intense sweating that can drench sleepwear and bedding. They disrupt sleep quality and can lead to insomnia, daytime fatigue, and irritability. Night sweats are caused by the same hormonal fluctuations that trigger hot flashes.
management: Avoid alcohol and heavy meals before bed
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If soaking through sheets nightly, especially with unexplained weight loss or lumps (could indicate lymphoma)

entries.title: Irregular Periods
entries.description: Changes in menstrual cycle pattern, flow, or duration
entries.content: Irregular periods are often the first sign of perimenopause. Changes can include shorter or longer cycles, heavier or lighter bleeding, skipped periods, or unpredictable timing. This occurs as the ovaries produce fluctuating levels of estrogen and progesterone and ovulation becomes irregular. Eventually, periods stop altogether, marking menopause after 12 consecutive months without menstruation.
management: Use appropriate menstrual products for flow changes
Consult doctor if bleeding is very heavy or prolonged
entries.when_to_see_doctor: Bleeding after menopause, periods lasting >7 days, cycles <21 days, very heavy bleeding, bleeding between periods

entries.title: Vaginal Dryness
entries.description: Reduced natural lubrication in the vagina causing discomfort
entries.content: Vaginal dryness occurs when declining estrogen levels cause the vaginal tissues to become thinner, less elastic, and produce less natural lubrication (vaginal atrophy). This can lead to itching, burning, discomfort, and pain during sexual intercourse (dyspareunia). It can also increase susceptibility to urinary tract infections.
entries.duration: Can persist throughout postmenopause if untreated
management: Use water-based or silicone-based lubricants during sex
Stay sexually active to increase blood flow
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If causing significant discomfort, pain during sex, or recurrent UTIs

entries.title: Sleep Disturbances
entries.description: Difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or poor sleep quality
entries.content: Sleep problems are very common during menopause, affecting up to 60% of women. Insomnia can be caused directly by hormonal changes affecting sleep regulation, or indirectly by night sweats, anxiety, or the need to urinate frequently. Poor sleep leads to daytime fatigue, irritability, difficulty concentrating, and reduced quality of life.
entries.duration: Can last throughout perimenopause and into postmenopause
management: Create cool, dark, quiet bedroom environment
Avoid caffeine and alcohol before bed
Exercise regularly but not close to bedtime
Treat underlying night sweats or anxiety
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If sleep problems persist despite lifestyle changes or severely impact daily functioning

entries.title: Joint Pain and Muscle Aches
entries.description: Stiffness, pain, or inflammation in joints and muscles
entries.content: Joint pain (arthralgia) and muscle aches are common during menopause, affecting hips, knees, hands, and shoulders. Declining estrogen levels contribute to inflammation and reduced joint lubrication. This can lead to stiffness, especially in the morning, and reduced mobility.
management: Regular exercise, especially low-impact activities (swimming, walking)
Maintain healthy weight to reduce joint stress
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If pain is severe, persistent, worsens at night, or occurs without activity (could indicate other conditions)

entries.title: Weight Gain
entries.description: Increased body weight, especially around the abdomen
entries.content: Weight gain during menopause averages 1.5 pounds per year through the 50s. Hormonal changes affect metabolism, appetite, and fat distribution, leading to increased abdominal fat even without changes in diet or exercise. Loss of muscle mass with aging also slows metabolism.
management: Balanced, nutrient-rich diet with portion control
Strength training to maintain muscle mass
Limit processed foods, sugar, and saturated fats
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If rapid or unexplained weight gain, especially with other symptoms

entries.title: Headaches and Migraines
entries.description: Increased frequency or severity of headaches
entries.content: Hormonal fluctuations during perimenopause can trigger or worsen headaches and migraines, especially in women with a history of migraines. Headaches often improve after menopause when hormone levels stabilize. However, new or worsening headaches after menopause warrant medical evaluation.
management: Maintain regular sleep and meal schedules
Hormone therapy may help or worsen (varies by individual)
entries.when_to_see_doctor: New headaches after menopause, severe headaches, headaches with fever/nausea/vision changes, or progressively worsening headaches

entries.title: Heart Palpitations
entries.description: Noticeable pounding, fluttering, or racing heartbeat
entries.content: Heart palpitations can occur during menopause due to hormonal changes affecting the cardiovascular system. While often benign, they can be alarming and should be evaluated to rule out cardiac conditions.
entries.when_to_see_doctor: Always see a doctor for palpitations to rule out heart conditions, especially if accompanied by chest pain, shortness of breath, or dizziness

entries.title: Urinary Urgency and Incontinence
entries.description: Increased need to urinate, difficulty controlling bladder
entries.content: Declining estrogen weakens pelvic floor muscles and urethral tissues, leading to urinary urgency (sudden strong need to urinate), frequency, and stress incontinence (leaking with coughing, sneezing, laughing). Also increases risk of urinary tract infections (UTIs).
management: Medications for overactive bladder if needed
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If accompanied by bloating, pelvic pain, feeling full quickly, or weight loss (could indicate ovarian cancer)

entries.title: Breast Tenderness
entries.description: Soreness, sensitivity, or pain in breasts
entries.content: Breast tenderness and swelling can occur during perimenopause due to hormonal fluctuations. This is similar to premenstrual breast tenderness but may be more pronounced. Symptoms typically improve after menopause.
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If severe, persistent, or accompanied by lumps, discharge, or skin changes

entries.title: Skin Changes
entries.description: Dry, thin, itchy, or less elastic skin
entries.content: Estrogen helps maintain skin hydration, collagen production, and elasticity. Declining estrogen leads to drier, thinner, more fragile skin that's prone to itching and wrinkles. Skin may also bruise more easily.
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If severe itching, rashes, or skin changes that don't improve

entries.title: Hair Thinning and Loss
entries.description: Reduced hair density, thinning, or hair loss
entries.content: Hormonal changes during menopause can cause hair thinning on the scalp and sometimes increased facial hair growth. This is due to the relative increase in androgens (male hormones) as estrogen declines.
management: Avoid harsh chemicals and heat styling
Balanced diet with adequate protein and iron
Biotin and other hair supplements (consult doctor)
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If sudden or severe hair loss

entries.title: Digestive Issues
entries.description: Bloating, gas, changes in bowel habits
entries.content: Hormonal changes can affect the gastrointestinal system, leading to bloating, gas, constipation, or changes in gut bacteria. Water retention and slower digestion are common during menopause.
management: Reduce salt intake to minimize bloating
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If persistent bloating with pelvic pain, feeling full quickly, or changes in elimination (could indicate ovarian cancer)

entries.title: Fatigue
entries.description: Persistent tiredness not relieved by rest
entries.content: Extreme fatigue is common during menopause, often resulting from poor sleep, hormonal changes, or other menopausal symptoms. It can significantly impact daily activities and quality of life.
management: Treat underlying sleep problems or depression
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If extreme fatigue not relieved by rest, especially with unexplained weight loss or other concerning symptoms

entries.title: Decreased Bone Density
entries.description: Weakening of bones increasing fracture risk (osteoporosis)
entries.content: Estrogen plays a crucial role in maintaining bone density. After menopause, women can lose up to 25% of bone mass by age 60, significantly increasing the risk of osteoporosis and fractures, especially in the spine, hips, and wrists.
entries.when_to_see_doctor: Fractures before menopause, family history of osteoporosis, or risk factors present

entries.title: Dry Mouth and Dental Issues
entries.description: Reduced saliva production, sensitive teeth, painful gums
entries.content: Hormonal changes can affect oral health, leading to dry mouth, burning mouth syndrome, sensitive teeth, and gum problems. This increases risk of cavities and gum disease.
management: Sugar-free gum or lozenges to stimulate saliva
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If severe or persistent oral symptoms

entries.title: Brittle Nails
entries.description: Weak, cracked, or easily broken nails
entries.content: Changes in keratin production during menopause can lead to brittle, weak nails that crack or break easily.
management: Avoid harsh chemicals and nail products
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If accompanied by other symptoms or severe changes

entries.title: Body Odor Changes
entries.description: Changes in sweat composition or body odor
entries.content: Hormonal fluctuations and increased sweating from hot flashes can change body odor during menopause.
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If sudden significant changes in body odor

entries.title: Dizziness
entries.description: Feeling lightheaded, faint, or unsteady
entries.content: Dizziness can occur during menopause due to hormonal effects on blood sugar regulation, blood pressure, or inner ear function. It can also be related to hot flashes or anxiety.
management: Eat regular meals to maintain blood sugar
Rise slowly from sitting or lying
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If frequent, severe, or accompanied by other symptoms like chest pain or vision changes

entries.title: Tingling Sensations (Paresthesia)
entries.description: Tingling, numbness, or 'pins and needles' in hands, feet, or other areas
entries.content: Some women experience tingling sensations (paresthesia) during menopause, possibly due to hormonal effects on the nervous system or changes in circulation.
management: Rule out other causes (diabetes, nerve compression)
entries.when_to_see_doctor: Always see a doctor to rule out other serious causes like diabetes or neurological conditions

entries.title: Electric Shock Sensations
entries.description: Brief, sudden sensations like an electric shock
entries.content: Some women report feeling brief electric shock sensations, often preceding a hot flash. This may be due to hormonal effects on the nervous system.
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If frequent or concerning

entries.title: Allergies and Sensitivities
entries.description: New or worsening allergies or sensitivities
entries.content: Hormonal changes can affect the immune system, leading to new allergies or worsening of existing ones. This is related to effects on IgE antibodies.
management: Maintain healthy immune system through diet and lifestyle
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If new severe allergies or anaphylaxis risk
